themes_detail.label: Street Signs Vanishing
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints spiked to 6 THIS WEEK—a 300% jump from the 1.5-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting either systematic theft, wind damage, or neglected maintenance that could create navigation and safety hazards across Greenpoint/Williamsburg.
evidence: 6 street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.5)
300% spike represents statistically significant deviation from baseline
No recent news or Reddit discussion of this issue, suggesting underreported problem
reporting_angles: Are signs being stolen by scrappers or vandals, or is the city failing to maintain them post-winter?
Interview DOT about maintenance schedules and whether they've noticed a trend

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints jumped to 5 THIS WEEK—a 700% spike from the 0.6-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—indicating potential tensions over sidewalk seating expansion, operating hours, or quality-of-life impacts in residential areas.
evidence: 5 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.41)
700% proportional spike coincides with warming weather and likely expansion of Open Streets/Open Restaurants permits
Aligns with long-running CB budget request for land use planning and traffic/pedestrian safety concerns
reporting_angles: Are newly reopened or expanded outdoor dining venues in Williamsburg/Greenpoint creating noise or sidewalk obstruction issues?
Interview residents and venue owners about post-winter expansion plans and friction points

themes_detail.label: Tree Health Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Tree-related complaints accelerated sharply LAST WEEK, with new tree requests at 2300% above baseline (3 vs. 0.1 weekly average) and dead/dying tree reports at 392% above baseline (8 vs. 1.6 weekly average), suggesting spring damage assessment or disease outbreak warranting city forestry investigation.
evidence: New Tree Requests: 3 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69, highest severity)
Dead/Dying Trees: 8 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average (z-score: 7.44)
Combined signal suggests post-winter or spring damage assessment phase, or possible disease/pest pressure
reporting_angles: Did winter storms damage trees significantly in the district, or is this an arborist-led assessment season?
Investigate whether there's a diseased tree outbreak (invasive species, pest) that would explain simultaneous death and replacement requests

themes_detail.label: Noise at Houses of Worship
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from houses of worship spiked to 3 THREE WEEKS AGO—a 700% jump from the 0.4-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—indicating either increased religious gatherings, amplified events, or neighbor tolerance thresholds being tested.
evidence: 3 noise complaints from houses of worship THREE WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.42)
700% proportional spike but timing is 3 weeks old—less urgent than this week's spikes
No follow-up complaints in most recent week, suggesting issue may be resolved or seasonal
reporting_angles: Were there specific holiday/religious observances that triggered elevated complaints three weeks ago?
Interview community board or police about any mediation efforts between congregations and neighbors

themes_detail.label: Miscellaneous Complaints Rise
themes_detail.summary: General category 311 complaints doubled THIS WEEK to 23 from an 11.1 weekly average—a 107% spike (z-score: 3.65)—suggesting either systemic service failures across multiple categories or residents increasingly frustrated with cumulative quality-of-life issues.
evidence: 23 general complaints THIS WEEK vs. 11.1 weekly average (z-score: 3.65)
107% spike in catchall category suggests either data coding shift or resident frustration with unresolved issues
Lacks specificity but timing is current
reporting_angles: Obtain detailed 311 logs to determine what issues are being lumped into 'general'—may reveal reporting system gaps
Interview 311 staff or city data team to understand if categorization methodology changed
